document.title: Unauthenticated adjacent command execution via HA

acknowledgments.summary: Internally discovered and reported by Theo Leleu of Fortinet Product Security team with the use of Frontier AI model: Claude Mythos.

notes.title: Summary
notes.text: Missing authentication for critical function in FortiOS

notes.title: Additional info
notes.text:
FortiGate HA clusters running FGCP (both active-passive and active-active) are also affected on vulnerable pre-fix versions. However, exploitation requires HA-segment adjacent attack vector.

In environments where the HA L2 segment is not fully trusted, on fixed versions, enable the following configuration:

FGCP HA (a-p or a-a):
config system ha
   set password <secret>
   set encryption enable
   set authentication enable
end

Standalone-config-sync without FGSP peers: 
Same as above


Standalone-config-sync with FGSP peers:
Same as above and


config system standalone-cluster
   set encryption enable
   set psksecret <secret>
end

Autoscale:
config system autoscale
   set psksecret <secret>
end

Virtual Patch named "FG-VD-61445.0day." is available in FMWP db update 26.082

remediations.details:
FortiOS 8.0: Upgrade to 8.0.1 or above
FortiOS 7.6: Upgrade to 7.6.8 or above
FortiOS 7.4: Upgrade to 7.4.13 or above
FortiOS 7.2: Upgrade to 7.2.14 or above
FortiOS 7.0: Migrate to a fixed release
A virtual patch is available. FortiGuard IPS signature package: Virtual Patch named "FG-VD-61445.0day." is available in FMWP db update 26.082

references.summary: A missing authentication for critical function vulnerability [CWE-306] in FortiOS may allow an unauthenticated attacker with HA FGSP + standalone-config-sync, or autoscale to execute command as super admin via crafted HA packets.
